text:
anya: quick follow-up to the slab rewrite RFC  thinking about long-lived fragmentation (the "fracture" case) and cheaper defrag before full gpu->cpu offload. propose two small pieces: a very-low-cost frag-score sampler per-tenant, and a tiny reconcile API from evictor -> runtime to attempt bounded local compaction. reactions?

zane: can you sketch the cost model? we should know when compacting is net-positive vs just offloading.

sam: agree on cost model. metrics: tokens-per-move (i/o + compute), avg reuse window, and expected evict latency hit. without that scanner will oscillate.

may: api sketch (very small):
```
reconcile_eviction(tenant, range_start, range_end, urgency="low", budget_ms=5) -> {status: "ok"|"skip"|"defer", scanned: "N", moved: "M", token: "uuid"}
cancel_reconcile(token) -> {cancelled: true}
```
sync when budget_ms <= 10, else enqueue async. return best-effort counters.

liam: backward compat: runtime that doesn't implement reconcile should return skip so evictor falls back to existing offload. keep default behavior identical.

harper: tail-latency risk if reconcile runs on critical path. must bind budget and only call when scheduler signals slack or from background worker. annotate calls with urgency.

anya: exactly. plan: evictor only calls reconcile inline for low-latency budgets (<5ms) when it detects headroom; otherwise it posts reconcile job to background queue. frag-score biases which subpages we try to compact first.

zane: how to implement frag-score cheaply? per-subpage counters are heavy. maybe sampling 1/256 alloc/free and increment an 8-bit counter per-subpage, with periodic decay. lightweight.

sam: sampling + uint8 counters + periodic decay is solid. cheap reads/writes and declines slowly so we get sticky hotspots. keep counters per-arena to prefer intra-arena coalesce.

may: multi-tenant fairness: expose tenant-weighted thresholds. reconcile should consult tenant_quota_available() and host_headroom; if not enough headroom return defer. else proceed.

liam: make reconcile idempotent and cancellable: return a token and support cancel_reconcile(token). if pages get evicted mid-reconcile, abort and report partial metrics.

harper: telemetry requirements: moved/scanned per-tenant, budget_ms vs actual_ms, p50/95/99 latency, cancellations, deferred counts. we'll need these before enabling broadly.

jess: i can bench: simulate churn (small alloc/free hot slabs) and run reconcile with budgets [1,5,20ms], compare throughput and offload rate. will post numbers here. :mag_right:

anya: rollout: feature-flagged reconcile shim in runtime, default off. local unit tests -> bench -> canary on Dedicated -> wider enable. config knobs for tenant thresholds.

zane: note: compaction can spike peak memory usage (temporarily holding source + target pages). reconcile must check host_free_headroom >= COMPACT_OVERHEAD or skip. prevents a tenant from DoSing host by defragging.

sam: add pseudocode for evictor decision:
```
if frag_score(range) < FRAG_TH: return SKIP
if host_headroom() < MIN_OVERHEAD: return DEFER
resp = reconcile(...)
if resp.status == "ok" and resp.moved > 0: use result
else: fallback_offload()
```
SDK helper: try_reconcile_then_offload(range) hides retries/backoff.

may: small API details: expose urgency buckets (background/low/urgent). budgets map to sync vs async. document that async results are pushed to reconciler telemetry stream.

liam: for safety, reconcile should never block > max_block_ms on critical threads. runtime will enforce preemption. also gate reconcile on tenant admission controller.

harper: also add a metric for memory-pressure-triggered reconcile vs opportunistic reconcile. helps analyze cause of defrags.

jess: bench update (WIP): early runs show with 5ms budget we get ~35% fewer offloads on synthetic churn, latency p99 unchanged. 1ms budget helps a bit but misses deeper fragmentation. will finish and share numbers.

anya: action items: jess -> finish bench and paste results (EOW). may -> PR with API proto + types. zane/sam -> cost model doc + suggested thresholds. harper -> telemetry list + dashboards. liam -> cancellation semantics + preemption model. i'll draft RFC addendum after we have bench numbers. ops-bot: schedule follow-up next eng-runtime sync.

ops-bot: Reminder: eng-runtime sync in 30m.

anya: thanks all. keeping reconcile opt-in and budgeted should let us reduce fragmentation without surprise host costs.
